title: The Stanford Training Program in ELSI Research
text:
This application is for continued support of a T32 research training program at Stanford University to develop
independent scholars who can conduct rigorous research on ethical, legal and social implications of genetics
and genomics (ELSI). Since 2016, with support of this T32 award, we have appointed 13 postdoctoral scholars
into the program, and 9 have completed their training. The goal of this renewal is to train 7 postdoctoral fellows
(including 5 new trainees) and to continue our successful contribution to the excellence of the ELSI research
communities.

title: Nano Electrospun Polymeric Biomaterial Scaffold for GBM Interstitial Immunotherapy
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain cancer with poor survival rates, even with current treatments like
surgery. This project uses a biodegradable material called acetalated dextran (Ace-DEX) to deliver an immune-
activating drug directly to the tumor site after surgery. The goal is to boost the body’s immune response against
the cancer while minimizing side effects, offering a new and more effective way to treat GBM.

title: Contribution of DNA replication to epigenetic inheritance in a model multi-cellular organism
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions): 
Asymmetric cell division (ACD) contributes to cellular diversity during development and adult tissue homeostasis 
because it produces two genetically identical cells with distinct fates influenced by the information they inherit. 
Failure to properly regulate these programs leads to many diseases such as tissue degeneration and cancer. In this 
project, I will provide insight into how DNA replication-coupled chromatin assembly generates asymmetries that 
underlie ACD in development and germline stem cells.

title: Defining the molecular interactions within nanoparticles that enable delivery of long nucleic acids
text:
Therapeutic use of CRISPR/Cas is currently limited by the lack of safe and effective delivery carriers that can
mediate gene editing in vivo to targeted tissues and cells. In this grant, we study recently developed Selective
ORgan Targeting (SORT) lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) that can mediate tissue-specific gene editing in the liver,
lung, and spleen. Outcomes of this work will include elucidating the fundamental mechanisms how and why
SORT LNPs target extrahepatic tissues, determining how SORT molecules control efficacy and tolerability for
improved gene editing, quantifying cell-type gene editing specificity to expand targeted gene editing, and
ultimately opening new avenues for CRISPR/Cas-based correction of genetic diseases by developing
efficacious, safe, and translatable nanoparticle carriers.

title: The Impacts of Consultants on Financial, Operational, and Quality Outcomes in the U.S. Health System
text:
Health care providers – particularly nonprofit health care delivery organizations – are increasingly turning to
consultants for financial and operational expertise; however, no empirical research has yet examined the costs
or impacts of these consultants. By creatively leveraging publicly available IRS tax filings for nonprofit health
care delivery organizations, using machine learning to identify consulting contracts, linking to health care- and
patient-level datasets, and applying causal inference methods, the proposed work will provide the first
assessment of consultants in the U.S. health system.

title: Family-centered Risk Information and Screening Education to Support Children with Genetic Cancer Risk
text:
Hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes affect 5-10% of patients with incident cancers, with heightened risk
among patients who develop cancer at a young age, especially children. As a result, genetic counseling and
testing is increasingly recommended for children with new cancer diagnoses so that screening for new cancers
can take place; however, no family-centered models for cancer risk communication have been developed. The
proposed study will develop and test a novel, patient- and family-centered model for cancer risk communication
to meet the unique needs of children with genetic cancer risk.

title: Shark Radiotherapy for the Treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
text:
Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly lethal subtype of breast cancer and there is an unmet need
to develop innovative, effective therapies to combat TNBC. Radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs) are in
development for nearly all forms of cancer, however, no FDA-approved RPTs exist for TNBC nor are there any
undergoing clinical trials. The goal of this project is to develop a clinically relevant therapeutic strategy using
targeted RPTs derived from sharks that will effectively and safely deliver therapeutic radionuclides to the tumor
resulting in an increased therapeutic index for RPTs and improved patient outcomes.

title: Automated speech assessment for diagnosis of FTD spectrum disorders
text:
Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) spectrum disorders represent one of the most common causes of dementia in
younger individuals but can be challenging to diagnose, resulting in high social and economic burden. FTD
often causes changes to a patient’s speech, which makes speech an ideal target for a digital tool to aid the
diagnosis of FTD. In this proposal, we outline a project to develop a digital technology that will use speech
recordings from a self-administered speech exam and provide predictions for abnormal speech characteristics
and FTD subtype using machine learning.

title: In vivo genome editing for cerebrovascular disorders
text:
Cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) is a major cause of neurodegeneration and stroke. This multi-PI project
uses an ACTA2 R179H genetic vasculopathy model to test gene editing as a therapy to restore vascular and
white-matter integrity and to develop imaging and behavioral biomarkers that guide translation to human trials.

title: Mapping the determinants of bedaquiline resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
text:
Bedaquiline (BDQ) is recently developed antibiotic that is used to treat extensively drug-resistant Mycobacterium
tuberculosis (Mtb). In this proposal, we will use saturating mutagenesis to create a comprehensive database of
mmpR loss-of-function mutations that lead to BDQ resistance. This database can be used together with whole-
genome or amplicon sequencing approaches to rapidly diagnose resistance in clinical isolates.

title: Combating melanoma with an attenuated bacterial therapeutic
text:
Despite great advancement in immunotherapy for melanoma, such as adoptive cell transfer therapy and
checkpoint blockade, the clinical outcomes remain less satisfactory due to a variety of factors that lessen
antitumor efficacy. By investigating the role and mechanism of a safe attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant
producing a tryptophan metabolite in modulating the suppressive tumor microenvironment and immunotherapy
resistance, the proposed research will define and establish this microbe as a novel immunomodulatory agent
that can be exploited to significantly improve current melanoma immunotherapy.

title: PHARMACOLOGICAL MODULATION OF PIEZO1 CHANNELS
text:
Pharmacological modulation of mechanosensitive Piezo ion channels could help treat numerous diseases such
as inflammation, pain, and hypertension. To expand the currently limited Piezo channel pharmacome, this
proposal will investigate structural mechanisms of Piezo1 activation by a small molecule agonist and leverage a
recently identified pharmacological binding site to rationally design novel modulators with improved properties.
Successful completion of this project will deepen our fundamental understanding of vertebrate
mechanosensation and uncover novel molecules with potential value for basic research and the clinic.

title: Advanced PET/MRI to quantify heterogeneity of HER2 and vasculature in HER2+ breast-to-brain metastasis prior to combination targeted and radiotherapy
text:
Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 positive (HER2+) breast cancer has a higher incidence of brain
metastases compared to other breast cancer subtypes and standard-of-care treatment is typically radiation and
systemic targeted HER2 therapy. The overall goal of this proposal is to integrate advanced molecular imaging
with [89Zr] trastuzumab- positron emission tomography (PET) of HER2 expression and dynamic contrast
enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of vascularity to assess treatment response to radiation following
quantification of targeted HER2 bioavailability and heterogeneity in HER2+ breast-to-brain metastasis.

title: Mechanisms of cancer immunotherapy-associated thrombosis
text:
Immunotherapy is one of the most important new approaches to cancer therapy to emerge over the last
several decades but is associated with unique side effects that often mimic immune diseases. Recent studies
have identified thrombosis (excessive blood clotting) as an important side effect of immunotherapy, however,
nothing is known about the underlying causes of blood clots in these patients. The goal of this application is to
define these mechanisms using patient samples and a mouse model of blood clots induced by immunotherapy.

title: Common Stem Cell of Origin for Junctional and Gastric Adenocarcinoma
text:
The molecular features of esophageal adenocarcinoma and intestinal gastric cancer suggest they are a single
disease from a common and unusual cell-of-origin. Therapeutics that target this common cell-of-origin could
contribute to strategies for the elimination of these lethal cancers.

title: Transcriptional Regulation of Dormancy and Emergence in Breast Cancer
text:
Breast cancer-related death primarily results from metastatic growth of disseminated cells. The goal of this
project is to identify gene regulation programs that are critical for metastatic outgrowth of breast cancer cells
and amenable to pharmacological inhibition to reduce metastatic burden in breast cancer patients.

title: South Texas Medical Scientist Training Program (STX-MSTP)
text:
The South Texas MSTP trains the next generation of physician scientists in an interdisciplinary
basic science training environment with translational science and bioinformatics components. The
South Texas MSTP emphasizes training in high quality clinical care and rigorous scientific
investigation while also developing leadership and communication skillsets.

title: Mechanisms of microridge protrusion morphogenesis on mucosal epithelial cells
text:
Many mucosal epithelial cells project elaborate protrusions on their apical surfaces, called microridges, which
help adsorb and retain mucus. The Sagasti lab has established a zebrafish model to investigate the
morphogenesis of these understudied protrusions, revealing novel mechanisms by which the actomyosin
cortex, cytolinkers, and intermediate filaments contribute to protrusion morphogenesis. Future work will
investigate how cortical contractility is temporally and spatially regulated to promote microridge
morphogenesis, and identify additional regulatory proteins that build the microridge cytoskeletal scaffold.

title: Restriction of Toxoplasma growth in human cells
text:
Toxoplasma gondii is an obligate intracellular pathogen that can cause serious disease in
immunocompromised individuals, such as AIDS patients, and fetuses, and is also a major cause of blindness
in otherwise healthy individuals. In this proposal we will determine the mechanisms by which stimulated
primary human cells inhibit Toxoplasma growth and how the parasite’s secreted effectors counteract these
mechanisms. This will provide valuable insights into how human cells detect and destroy Toxoplasma and how
Toxoplasma counteracts this, potentially leading to novel therapeutics and allowing prediction of the virulence
of specific Toxoplasma strains in humans.

title: Functional genomics of microglial phagocytosis for precision neuroimmune therapeutics
text:
This project aims to develop the first in vivo CRISPR KO genetic screening platform to identify genetic
regulators of phagocytosis in microglia, the brain resident macrophage, in the context of Alzheimer's disease.
By leveraging advanced hematopoietic stem cell gene editing, barcoding, and transplantation into disease
models, this research will uncover novel therapeutic targets to enhance microglial function and mitigate
cognitive decline in AD. The findings and methods developed here will have broad implications for
understanding the basic biology of tissue resident macrophages and diseases involving tissue-resident
macrophage phagocytosis, such as cancer and atherosclerosis.
